newsitem.title: USA: NASD panel files muni complaint against Calif firm.
newsitem.headline: NASD panel files muni complaint against Calif firm.

text.p: An NASD panel filed disciplinary charges against San Francisco-based Pacific Genesis Group, Inc. for alleged unfair price markups in muni bonds, a complaint obtained by Reuters on Monday says.

The National Association of Securities Dealer's district business conduct committee in San Francisco alleged in the three-page filing that the firm conducted 54 sales of muni bonds at unfair and unreasonable prices.
The complaint, signed by NASD district director Elisabeth Owens, said that NASD is launching formal proceedings, but has made no "findings" in connection with its charges.
The filing is against the firm, its president Arch Zellick, director Daniel Young, and former trader Gerald Porter, Jr.
The document says the firm, acting through Zellick, Young and Porter, did 54 sales of munis to customers at prices that violated Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board rule G-30.
That rule requires muni professionals to sell bonds at fair and reasonable prices.
Zellick, Young and Porter were unavailable for comment.
The NASD committee's complaint also said Zellick permitted four people at the firm sell munis without being registered as muni securities or general securities reps.

In September 1996, California state Treasurer Matt Fong called on the Securities and Exchange Commission and California's Attorney General to investigate nine minicipal securities transactions underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group.
Fong alleged that illegal payments of bond proceeds were made, that bond proceeds were used to retire private debts and that bond professionals failed to identify the actual project beneficiaries.
